title: Exocometary gas structure, origin and physical properties around β Pictoris through ALMA CO multitransition observations
question: What are the structure, origin and physical conditions (electron/H2 density, CO mass, exocometary ice content) of CO gas in the beta Pic debris disk, from ALMA CO J=2-1 combined with archival J=3-2?

data.bands: Band 6 (CO J=2-1) new; Band 7 (CO J=3-2) archival

what.value: Disk thermodynamical model: temperature profile (80 K at 50 AU, slope -0.8), C II density ~150 cm^-3 at 85 AU, C I column

evidence.quote: we assume the temperature radial profile predicted by (cite: Kral2016a), i.e. a power law with slope of $-0.8$, normalised to a value of 80 K at 50 AU.
Keplerian rotation around a 1.75 M$_{\odot}$ star (cite: Crifo1997)

what.value: Fractional dust luminosity 2.1e-3 and stellar luminosity 8.7 Lsun

evidence.quote: fractional luminosity $L_{\rm dust}/L_{\ast}$ of $2.1\times 10^{-3}$ around a star of 8.7 $L_{\odot}$ (cite: KennedyWyatt2014)

what.value: Disk PA 29.3 deg from scattered light

evidence.quote: corresponding to 29.3$^\circ$$^{+0.2}_{-0.3}$ (cite: Lagrange2012)

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and match CO cubes
recipe.method: CASA calibration, concatenation of ACA+12m, uvcontsub, CLEAN natural weighting; degrade 2-1 to 3-2 resolution

recipe.goal: Measure integrated fluxes and line ratio
recipe.method: Spatially integrate primary-beam-corrected moment-0 maps; ratio errors summed in quadrature

recipe.goal: Fit vertical disk structure (spine, scale height)
recipe.method: 1D Gaussian fits to vertical cuts at each midplane position (>5 sigma); H from deconvolving beam
key_parameters: 300 walkers, 500 steps; uniform priors |y_obs|<20 AU, FWHM_beam<FWHM<80 AU

recipe.goal: Map PV diagrams to orbital plane and derive H(R), T(R)
recipe.method: Keplerian PV-to-radius mapping; H vs R power law; T from hydrostatic equilibrium
assumptions: M*=1.75 Msun, mu=14, vertically isothermal, Keplerian

recipe.goal: Constrain inclination and tilt via chi2 grid
recipe.method: Model double-Gaussian of front/back flux fractions over grid of i and dPA

recipe.goal: NLTE line ratio modelling for electron and H2 density
recipe.method: Compare 3-2/2-1 ratios per PV spaxel with NLTE grid in (Tk, ne) / (Tk, nH2), assuming Kral temperature profile
key_parameters: mask highest 10% of ratios (>3.80); spaxels >4 sigma
assumptions: Optically thin CO, electrons as only colliders (upper limits)

recipe.method: Monte Carlo over flux samples (1e4) and line ratio samples (1e8), random (Tk,ne) on ratio contour, upper level population
Steady-state: CO destruction rate (photodissociation with shielding) divided by solid mass loss rate from collisional cascade
assumptions: Steady state; belt 50-150 AU; production rate is lower limit

evidence.quote: $(3.5\pm0.4) \times10^{-20}$ W m$^{-2}$ for the J=2-1 transition
$(6.7\pm0.7) \times10^{-20}$ W m$^{-2}$ for the J=3-2 transition
indicating an integrated 3-2/2-1 line ratio of $1.9\pm0.3$
T=\left(2.1^{+0.4}_{-0.4} \times 10^{2}\right) \times \left(\frac{R}{85 \rm AU}\right)^{-1.58}
the formal best-fit (i.e. the $\chi^2$ minimum) is at $i\sim88^{\circ}$ and dPA $\sim3^{\circ}$
our measurements can confidently constrain the electron density in the disk to around $10^2$-$10^3$ cm$^{-3}$
its density would be between 10$^3$ and 10$^5$ cm$^{-3}$ at radii between 50 and 200 AU
corresponds to an excitation temperature $T_{\rm exc}=12\pm4$ K
The CO mass range obtained is $3.4^{+0.5}_{-0.4} \times 10^{-5}$ M$_{\oplus}$
we obtain an optical thickness $\tau_{3-2}=0.27\pm0.05$
we estimate a photodissociation timescale in the clump midplane of $\sim$300 years
yields a CO mass loss rate of 0.11 M$_{\oplus}$/Myr
The resulting total mass loss rate from the planetesimal belt is 1.9 M$_{\oplus}$/Myr
we obtain an upper limit of 6% on the CO mass abundance
The timescale for CO-C II collision obtained is 0.19 years
